intended_object: The weights (characters) of the rank-r diagonal torus t ↦ diag(t₀,…,t_{r-1},1) of PGL_{r+1}, acting by conjugation on the matrix units: at E_{ij} the weight is ε_i − ε_j in ℤ^r, with ε_r = 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses `finProdFinEquiv` to turn the index `a` into a pair `(i, j)` in `Fin (r+1) × Fin (r+1)`. It returns `diagonalLiftWeight i − diagonalLiftWeight j`. Here `diagonalLiftWeight k` is the standard basis vector e_k when k is one of the first r indices, and 0 when k is the last index r. So the weight at E_{ij} is ε_i − ε_j with ε_r = 0.

This is the right answer: conjugating by diag(s₀,…,s_{r-1},1) multiplies E_{ij} by s_i/s_j. The library confirms this in two ways:
- `mkQuotient_comp_diagonalTorusCoordinateMap` shows that the conjugation coordinate map equals the weight-torus map built from these weights.
- `torusCharacter_diagonalTorusWeight` evaluates the character at E_{ij} to the ratio of the i-th and j-th normalized diagonal coordinates.

Every edge case is covered: diagonal units get weight 0, and units in the last row or column get ±ε_i. The definition is a specific object tied to PGL_{r+1}, its matrix-unit representation and this torus parametrization, so it is not too narrow. The universe lift `ULift` is only there to make the universes fit. Mathlib has no counterpart.
